rows: 8,000 tents (~32,000 souls); ~8,500 riders (4 Wind Wings, 2 Lancer Banners, Iron-Girdle cataphracts, 120-rider keshik); remount strings 60,000+; the Silent Blade; nine banner-khans; the Sky-Banner

Three houses (Evereska, Cormanthor verge, Waterdeep factor-house); ~140 personnel; elven-community intelligence net (every elven death generates their paperwork); Sylrieth's strike crew (5 wardens + beast-handler pair); brokered stock (rust-swarm, nishruu, phase-hunters); bought empire clerk Thalos Wren (vault documentation chain); Sehanine charter; Evermeet legal cover.

Strike two in preparation against the Vitki-01 binding window (vault / binding / trio shakedown — loud public incident pending). Maintaining lawful consortium face; enforcement via brokered monsters, deniable.

Standing adversarial presence, never kill-locked; multiple stable outcomes.

Riding the heresy-text discovery: standing rising toward the twelfth seat, scholar's authority ascending at Sorcere, martial reputation building through seeded capture-doctrine authorship. Warm Bed Phases II–III window.

River city governed by elected Waterbaron. ~6,000 pop. Isle de Troll dragon-capture installation sits north of Yartar; Surbrin Eastern Road connects. Baen infrastructure directly adjacent. Waterbaron's cooperation or tolerance relevant to Isle de Troll operations.

Not military — magical. Individual Runemasters are CR 17+. Full council action is campaign-ending force. Strength is in secrecy and infiltration, not direct confrontation. ~100 outer-ring agents, ~30 inner ring, nine-member Runemasters' Council.
Horizon threat approaching via a multi-vector activation framework. First material contact expected ~mid-1494 DR via decoded Margaster architecture (Vector B).
Secret cabal of undead spellcasters founded 864 DR. NOT a current-arc antagonist — horizon threat. Shi'van cannot fight them at current level.
Mithral Hall fortress-hold, Gutbuster Brigade, mithral mining, Long Road trade, Gauntlgrym tool procurement partnership

Dwarven kingdom. ~10,000 pop. Commercially Allied with Baen/Gauntlgrym (tool procurement, NRTC-Dolgrin logistics, Einar envoy). Non-belligerent re Aldric Cold War. Fortress-hold insulation makes this sustainable.
~30 veteran soldiers. Mixed arms — longswords, shields, bows. Former Silverguard training. High unit cohesion, no cavalry, light armour (chain + leather). Scouts deployed on the Dessarin road.
Running a toll operation on the Stone Bridge–Yartar road; wintering in the collapsed Chauntea temple.
Dessarin corridor toll operation controlling the supply route to Ravencrest. Recruitable if the unit stays together.

~18 deployed operatives as isolated cells across the Sword Coast, Western Heartlands, Sembia and the Cormyrean court. Each CR 10–12, stealth/infiltration/assassination focus. No cohesive force capability; no production or training capacity since Naxxramas.
Decapitated and leaderless. Isolated cells continuing standing assignments with no command authority above them. Veil counter-program is a multi-year standing operational priority.
Mephistopheles's intelligence apparatus, named in deliberate parallel to Lirien's Veil as a calculated insult. Decapitated Uktar 1498 DR by the Bloodaxe Naxxramas operation.

Eleven delegate seats; combined dale militias (no unified command); the thirteen-century Compact with Cormanthor (Cormanthyri side held by Elara Baen'del from exile); control of the trade roads through the Dales; ~602,000 population across the eleven dales.

Watching Tethford. The Blue Hour negotiation outcome is the pattern the other ten dales will model. Some dales are Baen casus-belli targets; others intend to stay neutral. Council cannot act as one body — which is exactly what Sembian commercial pressure and Zhentarim cells both exploit.

Umbrella coordinating body for the eleven dales — not a government. Each dale keeps its own territory, government, militia, and trading pacts. No capital. Convenes annually at Midwinter, one delegate per dale, in a selected Dalelands town. Deliberative only: debates trade-road maintenance, common defense against Zhentarim and Sembian pressure, inter-dale border disputes, and Cormanthor/Compact matters. Two historical unification attempts failed (Aencar the Mantled King, slain 1044 DR). Campaign relevance: corridor Section B requires dale-by-dale consent; there is no single signature that clears the Dalelands.
~8,000 Jade Guard + 2,000 Eastern Reach border troops. The Office of Jade Correspondence — a 2,000-year intelligence service operating under diplomatic cover.
Active succession crisis — who follows Solanthei. Reform Council pressing for constitutional transition.
Eastern elven kingdom near Kara-Tur, 180K population. Celestine bloodline monarchy — the Jade Throne literally glows for a true Dreamer ruler.

Rule of Avernus (Layer 1, Blood War front line); the legal jurisdiction every soul-transaction into the Hells passes through first; contract leverage over Baen production scheduling; Section 7(J) embargo weaponized against Mammon's hierarchy.

Taking Warborn delivery on schedule. Avernus functions as friendly jurisdiction for imperial operations — Operation Sky Island stages Skyreach Castle through Avernus first before flying it against Dis. Contract quality faults and soul-binding anomalies carry infernal-standing implications, not merely commercial ones.

Archduchess of Avernus, Lord of the First. Counterparty to the Zariel Warborn Contract — the single largest revenue commitment in campaign history. Priority contract 21,680,000 gp (5,000-unit priority order); full agreement potential 800M+ gp across 200,000 units; projected 747,000 gp/mo profit at scale. Contract holder is Arik Baen directly — revenue bypasses NCF and all subsidiary structures. Legal framework sits under the Asmodeus umbrella contract with a no-predation clause and Warborn extension clauses from the Hell Siege aftermath. Section 7 Subsection J carries a Mammon-exclusion clause keyed to the Storm Lord's grievance over Vasuvius.

The Dawn-Ankh in the Sun-Vault (compact anchor). Economy: high-grade saltpeter (one of few regional sources), sun-bronze, Imaskari artifact licensing, refined grains.

Independent polity at pre-contact temporal state. Storm Crown contact imminent; Arik has not committed to an approach (alliance-first / coerced vassalage / conquest — Lirien has explicitly recommended against conquest). Veil parallel operation (Veshira, Mulhan-scholar cover at Sethr-Anhepet) proceeds regardless. Strategic objective: the Akhet-Senet plateau, Thay-held since ~1100 DR.

Kingdom of self-aware undead and their living allies in the depopulated corridor between Thay's northern frontier and the Anauroch desert margin (~250 mi E-W, 70-100 mi N-S). Founded ~140 years ago by Mehura Anhepset, the Sunless Queen, last priestess of the Dawn Mother, at Akhet-Sereth after the Time of Troubles. Capital Sethr-Anhepet. ~80,000 souls: ~35,000 sapient Awakened (full legal citizens) + ~30,000 living + ~20,000 military. Governance: theocratic monarchy under the Sunless Queen, with the Council of First Awakened (23 founders, territorial responsibility, advisory) and the Living Council (31 elected, advisory but consent REQUIRED for trade, agriculture, marriage law, and refugee settlement).

No formal military. Potential civic militia growing to paramilitary through Robb Stark's training (5-stage escalation). Currently a political movement, not an armed force.
Channeling refugee-crisis grievance into xenophobic political organising; recruitment pressure on Institut hiring and Edmund's community.

Rule of Dis (Layer 2); the Iron Tower (regeneration anchor); the Iron Rod; layer-wide scrying and telepathy; custody of the Hells' contract archive — every infernal pact drafted, sealed, and stored; summons that never fail within his own city.

Standing target of Operation Sky Island (design canon, forward-horizon). Does not yet know he is one. The operation revokes his escape via Maltheus reality anchors BEFORE breaching the Iron Tower; the prize is custody, not a kill — boxing him in orichalcum as a permanent unspent asset on a decaying ~1,400-year true-name-fragment binding.

The Iron Duke, Lord of the Second, ruler of Dis — the Iron City. The most cautious archdevil in the Hells; has not left the top of his Iron Tower in an age. Defining traits: self-only greater teleport always loaded (his entire survival architecture), divine rank 0 (regenerates from the Iron Tower if killed within Dis), greater rust (un-equips opponents before a blow lands), layer-wide telepathy, continuous true seeing, perpetual mind blank. He does not fight — cornered, he bargains. Honest within the letter of a sealed contract, treacherous on every syllable outside it. Dis is where infernal pacts are drafted, sealed, and stored, making him the Hells' great fence, banker, and contract-broker.
Purple Dragons (~12,000), War Wizards (arcane military intelligence), Forest Kingdom, noble houses, Suzail capital

~45 mixed combatants (veterans, criminals, displaced farmers). Fortified hilltop camp — stone walls, timber palisade, watchtower. Mounted scouts (Serena's 6 rangers). Infantry with military weapons and mixed armour.
Being squeezed south by Bloodaxe Legion northern operations; the Ravencrest claim puts a landowner directly in Dunbarrow's path.
Greypeak foothills, ~40 miles north of Ravencrest. Pressured south by the Bloodaxe Legion. Not recruitable as a unit.
10,000 refugees including a functioning government-in-exile bureaucracy; some military capability; integrated into Arik's Northern Kingdom infrastructure.
Consolidating the exile court under Queen Elara Baen'del; managing legitimacy pressure from the rival True Cormanthor court.
